tool_call_format: harmony channels: tool defs rendered as a TypeScript namespace in the developer message; a call is '<|start|>assistant to=functions.NAME<|channel|>commentary json<|message|>{args}<|call|>'; a result is '<|start|>functions.NAME to=assistant<|channel|>commentary<|message|>"{result}"<|end|>' (result JSON-encoded)
thinking_toggle: none: the template never reads enable_thinking or thinking; reasoning is a 'Reasoning: <reasoning_effort>' line in the system message (default medium). Disabling thinking is server-side (reasoning_budget_tokens=0).
known_template_errors: assistant content containing '<|channel|>...<|message|>' raises 'You have passed a message containing <|channel|> tags in the content field...' (b11960 patches this check to '{%- if false %}' in common_chat_templates_init)
a tool message with no preceding assistant tool call raises 'Message has tool role, but there was no previous assistant message with a tool call!'
a second or later tool_calls entry in one assistant message is silently dropped: the template renders only message.tool_calls[0]
an empty messages list raises UndefinedError (messages[0] is read unconditionally)
a developer message that is not messages[0] is silently dropped; only the first developer/system message becomes '# Instructions'
notes: Both gpt-oss models ship the identical template (sha256 a4c9919cbbd4acdd51ccffe22da049264b1b73e59055fa58811a99efbd7c8146). effort values are interpolated verbatim and never validated, so every level renders, but the model was trained on low/medium/high only; 'none' is intercepted by the server before the template (server-common.cpp:1497-1504 erases the kwarg and sets enable_thinking=false, which this template ignores), so 'none' does NOT shorten reasoning. b11960 detects supports_parallel_tool_calls=false from this template. Tool-call arguments must be an object; a JSON string is double-encoded by |tojson unless llama.cpp's func_args_not_string normalization runs.
